headline: The wheel took thousands of years to invent—simple doesn't mean obvious
universal_truth: Some ideas seem obvious in hindsight but required genius to discover
fun_facts: The wheel was invented around 3500 BCE—thousands of years after humans built pyramids
Wheels were first used for pottery, not transportation
The Americas never invented the wheel for transportation, despite having rolling toys
discussion_questions: Why do you think the wheel took so long to invent?
What 'obvious' ideas might we be missing today?
What makes some inventions harder to discover than others?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The wheel seems obvious—round things roll. But humans built cities, wrote languages, and raised pyramids for thousands of years before inventing the wheel. Simple doesn't mean easy to discover. The wheel took genius.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If rolling is natural—logs roll, balls roll—why did the wheel take so long to invent? What made this 'simple' idea so hard to discover?
cliff.prompt: Why was the wheel hard to invent?

options.text: The wheel is useless alone—it needs an axle, and that combination is hard to figure out
options.response: Yes. A wheel without an axle just rolls away. The wheel-and-axle system requires precision and insight—two inventions at once.

options.text: People didn't need wheels before they had things to transport
options.response: Need existed, but the technical challenge was the wheel-axle system...

q1.title: Pottery First
q1.script: The first wheels weren't for carts—they were potter's wheels, spinning clay into vessels. Transportation wheels came later. The same principle—rotation on an axis—found its first use in art, not travel.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Pottery First"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Two-Part Puzzle
q2.script: A wheel is useless without an axle that fits precisely—too tight and it won't turn, too loose and it wobbles. This two-part system required solving multiple problems simultaneously. That's why it took millennia.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Not Universal
q3.script: The Americas had wheel-like toys but never developed wheeled vehicles. Why? Possibly no suitable draft animals, or terrain better suited to waterways. Context shapes what inventions emerge. Need plus capability equals invention.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Obvious in hindsight doesn't mean obvious in foresight. The wheel teaches humility—ideas that seem simple required genius to discover. What 'obvious' ideas are we missing today?
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 112. Tomorrow, we'll explore how levers multiply force. Until then, appreciate that something as 'simple' as the wheel represents a breakthrough of human ingenuity.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Hindsight Humility - Appreciate Discovery
growTrack.learning_objective: Develop appreciation for the difficulty of innovation
growTrack.activity: Think of something you consider 'obvious.' Now imagine you lived before it existed. Would you have invented it? The wheel, zero, the scientific method—all were breakthroughs that seem inevitable only after they happened.
